items.title: Nexus: Depth-Adaptive KV-Cache Splicing and Retrieval-Decoupled Tool Routing for Agentic LLMs on Unified Memory
items.one_liner: Highly relevant for developers building high-performance LLM agents with large toolsets on unified memory hardware.
items.summary: Nexus is a framework designed to reduce the time-to-first-token (TTFT) for agentic LLMs using the Model Context Protocol (MCP) by decoupling tool routing from schema prefill costs. It uses an INT8 semantic lookaside buffer for tool selection and generates arguments over compressed signatures rather than full spliced KV caches. While KV cache splicing is used, it is limited by RoPE phase drift, which Nexus manages with a depth-adaptive suffix redecode. The system achieves significant TTFT speedups and context savings while maintaining output fidelity.
items.bottom_line: Decoupling tool routing from full schema prefill allows agents to scale to hundreds of tools without the quadratic latency penalty of traditional context loading.

claims.text: Nexus decouples tool routing from schema-prefill costs using a semantic lookaside buffer.
claims.support_span: Nexus's primary lever is to decouple routing from the schema-prefill cost: an INT8 semantic lookaside buffer (SLB) with a calibrated cross-encoder margin gate selects tools by retrieval

claims.text: It achieves a 1.1-1.7x TTFT speedup at moderate context depths.
claims.support_span: the resulting never-regress property is a guarantee on output fidelity... alongside a 1.1-1.7x TTFT speedup at moderate depth

claims.text: Routing accuracy remains near 89% even with 250 tools.
claims.support_span: routing accuracy stays near 89% as the registry scales to 250 tools

items.title: Representation Affects Retrieval: A Case Study of Skill Discovery and Routing in a Multimodal Agent Harness
items.one_liner: Practical insight for prompt engineering and tool-calling architecture in agentic systems.
items.summary: This case study of the Tinycloud multimodal agent harness explores how the representation of skills in system prompts affects an LLM's ability to select the correct tool. The research found that providing full instructions (inlined-body) for all skills ensures correct selection but can lead to lexical competition where similar names cause misrouting. Conversely, omitting skill details leads to discovery failures and slower execution. The study concludes that in-prompt exposure is not monotonically helpful and requires careful management of lexical signals.
items.bottom_line: More information in an agent's prompt does not always improve performance; lexical collisions between tool descriptions can actively cause the model to misroute tasks.

claims.text: Full autoloading of skills selects the correct skill but can create lexical competition.
claims.support_span: a six-task selection ablation across three exposure regimes (all-on, default, all-off) shows that full autoload selects the gold skill on every task... partial exposure can create lexical competition that suppresses correct selection.

claims.text: The production default misrouted a task due to lexical signal collision.
claims.support_span: the production default misroutes one task because its lexical signal collides with an autoloaded tool-skill that pulls planner attention away from a listed workflow-skill.

items.title: UAT-10147: Chinese-speaking adversary integrates agentic AI into post-compromise operations
items.one_liner: First major report of a threat actor operationalizing agentic AI for end-to-end intrusion workflows.
items.summary: Cisco Talos has identified a Chinese-speaking threat actor, UAT-10147, that is actively using agentic AI to automate post-compromise operations. The group targets Windows and Linux web servers globally, using AI for reconnaissance, payload generation, and iterative exploit refinement. Talos observed the actor using tools like PentestGPT and DeepAudit to scale complex attacks and generate operational playbooks. This represents a shift from simple AI-assisted scripting to semi-autonomous offensive orchestration, allowing lower-skilled actors to perform advanced intrusions.
key_facts: Sectors: Government, education, media, tech, gaming
items.bottom_line: Real-world threat actors are now using agentic AI frameworks to automate the entire post-exploitation lifecycle, significantly lowering the barrier to entry for complex cyberattacks.

items.title: Q1 earnings cheer needs to last, but it may not
items.one_liner: Provides a critical perspective on the sustainability of the Indian market rally amidst global skepticism.
items.summary: India has become the least-favored stock market in Asia according to a BofA Securities survey, cited for weak growth and high valuations. While Q1FY27 earnings showed a 4% growth for Nifty 50 companies, analysts warn that this recovery may not be sustainable without a pick-up in domestic manufacturing. High crude oil prices and a sub-par monsoon season remain significant risks to future profitability. The market currently trades at a premium compared to other emerging markets, putting pressure on companies to deliver consistent earnings.
items.bottom_line: Despite positive Q1 results, structural headwinds and high valuations are making global investors cautious about Indian equities.
